slides.texte_overlay:
Skills that will make you
unforgettable at work
Learn to explain your job in one sentence. Not the title. "I help small shops get more customers online." People remember a clear sentence long after they've forgotten a fancy job title.
Learn to make other people look good. In the meeting, say "Sarah found that, it was a great catch." Giving credit costs you nothing, and people never forget who did it in front of the boss.
Learn to run a short meeting. Agenda in the invite, start on time, end five minutes early. "That's all we needed, have your time back." People will genuinely love you for those five minutes.
Have something interesting to say at lunch. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. While everyone talks about traffic, you're the one with the strange story that gets the whole table talking.
slides.texte_sophia: Have something interesting to say at lunch. While everyone talks about traffic, you've got the story. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app makes it easy, five minutes a day of history, art or science.

slides.texte_overlay: Learn to bring solutions, not just problems. "The client's upset. Here's what I think we should do." Anyone can spot a problem. The one who walks in with a fix is the one people remember.
Learn to welcome new people. Show the new guy where the coffee is, invite him to lunch on day one. Everyone remembers who was kind to them in their first awkward week, sometimes for years.
Learn to say thank you properly. Not "thx." Say "Thanks for staying late on Friday, it really saved the launch." Specific thanks is rare at work, and it's the kind people actually remember.
